name: Mark's Occult
description: Quirky consumer technology, paranormal gadgetry, horror gaming, and all things that lie beyond the veil -- all in one convenient space

name: Martin Killmann
description: Martin Killmann's newsletter is mainly about tabletop RPG design, including a running series on choosing dice mechanics and building systems.

name: Massimog’s Massiblog
description: Massimo Gauthier's blog mostly follows the development of his game Diorama Break, with occasional posts on game analysis, programming and unrelated topics.

name: MassivelyOP
description: Every gamer wants to be Massively Overpowered! Independent MMORPG news and opinions

name: Matt Horton
description: Matt Horton's personal blog collects his writing on video games, comics and the tech he uses, alongside notes on his YouTube work.

name: Mavro
description: Site no longer exists

name: Meaningful Gameplay
description: Eileen Seemann, a game designer who has worked on titles including Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora and Forge of Empires, writes about how psychology, neuroscience and emotional design shape games.

name: Mechanized Narrative
description: Essays by a former game writer and narrative designer (co-writer of Inkle's Sorcery Parts 3 and 4) on how mechanics and story intersect in video games, with a focus on JRPGs, tactics games and 1990s titles.

name: Mediavania
description: The Substack newsletter for Mediavania, a site that collects and surfaces writing about games from across the web.

name: Medium Quality
description: Adam McDorman writes long-form essays about the video games he plays, often RPGs.

name: Metal & Games
description: This is a Metal and Video Game Publication, will mostly equally look at both topics, If you like either of those things you found a right place

name: Mike Berger Games
description: Hi there! I'm a gamer and mental health profession. Consider this part blog, part journalism, and part info driven substack. I'll try to make you laugh too. "try"

name: Milk and Pixels
description: Nina Koch's devlog for My Significant Otter, a pixel-art digital pet game, and the brick-breaker Milk and Pixels, covering progress, pixel art and development alongside parenting.

name: Mindful Gamer
description: Reflective essays on play, game design and psychology, looking at how games shape the way people grow, feel and see the world.

name: Mostly Normal Monthly
description: Your monthly dose of gaming pontification from the hosts of the Mostly Normal Gamers Podcast!

name: Multiplier
description: A column about the conversation happening in games, with a focus on Australia and Australian game development.

name: Museum of Screens
description: A blog about web and browser games, past and present, with a recurring Web Game of the Day feature and longer pieces on the history and culture of Flash-era and itch.io games.

name: Narrative Game Reports
description: A narrative designer focused on analyzing games and their philosophy, development style, and design choices

name: Narrative News
description: A newsletter about narrative design in video games, with articles, how-tos and interviews with game writers plus a monthly round-up of jobs and resources for narrative designers.

name: Nathalie Lawhead
description: The blog of Nathalie Lawhead, a net-artist and independent game designer, with essays on experimental games, tools, the indie scene and digital culture.

name: Nerd Cave Newz
description: Gaming news without the PR spin. You get real context, straight talk, and breakdowns of what industry decisions actually mean for players, informed by more than a decade of covering games and watching the same trends repeat.

name: Nerd Central
description: John Murphy's commentary on a lifetime with video games, revisiting classics, questioning modern trends and reviewing games, films and other geek culture.

name: Neverending Backlog
description: Too many games, not enough time. In this Substack you will find reviews, discussions and opinions for video games as I slowly move through my backlog.

name: NewArteest Developments
description: Joe Hocking, a Chicago-area game programmer and author of Unity in Action, blogs about his current projects, including technical devlog posts on his tactical RPG and tips for Unity and Godot.

name: Nintendo is Great
description: A beautiful, trenchant journey playing every game for every Nintendo console/handheld library. We proceed in (mostly) chronological order.

name: No Escape
description: Kaile Hultner's site, subtitled Digital Culture and its Discontents, publishes reviews, impressions and play diaries of video games alongside essays on games culture.

name: No Time to Game
description: Dorian, a former TV news producer turned games writer, covers video game news, interviews, reviews and events, with an emphasis on game stories and the people who make and play them.

name: Not Public Opinion
description: Site no longer exists

name: Novecento's Tome of Odds
description: Novecento's newsletter about RPGs, tabletop games and video games, with news on their own game releases, articles about running games and reviews.

name: ORD
description: OnlineRaceDriver covers virtual motorsport across sim racing and arcade racing games, with news, updates, hardware coverage and buying guides, led by Dan Thornton with contributors.

name: Observations of the Fox
description: A long-running blog by designer Vulpinoid about tabletop roleplaying game design, play reports, worldbuilding and self-published RPG projects such as Sceletus.

name: Obsidian Moonshine
description: The personal blog of writer and podcaster Noah Chan (Irothtin), with essays on video games alongside posts about anime, books and other media, plus Let's Play projects.

name: Obsolete Sony
description: Embark on a journey through the obscure world of forgotten, odd, and obsolete Sony devices.

name: OldManGaming’s Substack
description: Gareth, a UK-based PC and handheld gamer, writes about the games industry and games old and new, aiming for data-driven, well-sourced opinion pieces.

name: On Video Games
description: In-depth video game analysis and criticism from a game developer, focused on individual games, specific features and design philosophies.

name: Other Strangeness
description: The personal site of merritt k, a writer, comedian and game designer formerly of Fanbyte, who co-founded the studio In Secret Places; it carries her comics, essays and project news.

name: Over Powered Game Marketing
description: A blog by an indie game marketer and CEO of Frostbloom on how small developers can market their games and get them noticed.

name: OverkillWTF
description: Kevin Wammer's blog overkill.wtf (formerly cliophate.wtf) carries commentary on his hobbies and obsessions, including reading notes and link posts.

name: Oyito's Game Hub
description: Oya, a game tester and localisation specialist based in Spain, writes personal impressions and reviews of indie games, RPGs and co-op games.

name: Painted Pixels
description: Site no longer exists

name: Papaya Pants Studios Blog
description: Site no longer exists

name: Past Meets Pixel
description: Co-edited by Christopher Gerteis and Leroy King, Past Meets Pixel publishes analyses, reviews and articles on how video games engage with history, bridging academic research and games.

name: Patrick Curry
description: Site no longer exists

name: Pentadact
description: The blog of Tom Francis, designer and writer at Suspicious Developments (Gunpoint, Heat Signature, Tactical Breach Wizards), with posts on game design and running an indie studio.

name: Phones and Joysticks
description: Site no longer exists

name: Pixel Explorers Club
description: "It's like a book club, but for lil indie games." A community for curious indie game lovers, here to remind you to press pause and play – join us! Curated by HelloMissPotter.

name: Pixel Fix
description: A hit of gaming culture that cuts retro with modern and injects it straight into your eyeballs. Dealing out of Aotearoa, New Zealand.

name: Pixel Poppers
description: I look deeply and read closely. I connect dots and apply information from fields including art theory, psychology, and economics. I break down game mechanics and design decisions at least as much as I analyse story beats and character motives

name: Pixel Shift
description: Mario writes about video games, board games, films and other pop culture, including retrospectives on games remembered from childhood.

name: PixelRyu: Building Mobile Games Solo PixelRyu: Building Mobile Games Solo
description: Ryu, a solo mobile game developer in Tokyo, keeps a devlog on shipping puzzle games with Godot and AdMob, sharing revenue figures, post-mortems and progress on the horror game HOTARU: The Lost House.
